speaker: Doctor
text:
I am Dr. Agent. I see you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; could you tell me when these symptoms first started and if they have been getting worse over time?

Also, have you noticed any redness, warmth, or a bump on the finger, and does the pain worsen when you try to straighten it?

Please describe any recent injuries or repetitive activities you've been doing with that hand.

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That sounds like a significant hyperextension injury; did you hear a "pop" at the time of the accident, and can you currently make a fist with your right hand?

REQUEST IMAGES: Right hand X-ray (AP, Lateral, Oblique)
REQUEST TEST: Physical exam for joint stability and neurovascular status

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Extensor tendon avulsion at the distal phalanx).

The clinical presentation of an inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint after a hyperextension injury, combined with localized swelling and a normal X-ray, is classic for a mallet finger. The MRI is likely confirming the tendon disruption.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
